notes: The site was found at the published coordinates: a protected rectangle south-west of Kalibangan village holding two mounds, the western (KLB-1) about 125 m by 280 m and the eastern (KLB-2) about 270 m by 390 m, separated by a north-south valley with a track. Zoom 19 is not available here; all imagery is zoom 18 (0.52 m per pixel). Points are measured on Wayback release 8432 (first used 2021-07-21; acquisition date not given by the tools), whose low sun shows the relief best; releases 16749, 47471, 64776, 32553, 52304, 26334 and the current Vantor Vivid image (20260301) were viewed for identification, release 16749 showing the excavated house block most clearly. No feature on the plan survives as standing masonry, so every point is class C. The 1968-69 plan of the same site (iar6869_p0037) was read for context: it shows that the hatched KLB-2 west wall of this plan is the exposed middle stretch of a longer wall. While reading the IAR 1967-68 text for context (PDF page index 50) we saw a phrase describing the largest Harappan platform in the south of KLB-1 as 'east-west oriented', and the excavated house block in KLB-2 as adjoined by 'two north-south streets and an east-west connecting lane'; the text extract also ran into the first paragraph of PDF page index 51 (the KLB-2 fortification wall on the western periphery, exposed over 150 m, 3 to 3.9 m wide), and we read no further Kalibangan text; on the preceding pages the Tilwara and Bagor entries describe a cutting and a burial as running roughly east-west. No other orientation statement was seen.
